topIssues.title: interop: expiry-boundary restatements are one second stricter than the normative Message Expiry Invariant
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
The interop message-expiry boundary is stated three times across the interop specs, and the two summary restatements disagree with the normative definition by one second. Both production implementations follow the normative definition.

## Normative definition

[`specs/interop/messaging.md` § Message Expiry Invariant](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/2049036afe878a7cb443f513f4e6ca453d90c340/specs/interop/messaging.md?plain=1#L153-L163):

> The expiry invariant invalidates inclusion of any executing message with
> `id.timestamp + EXPIRY_TIME < executing_block.timestamp`

⇒ a message executed **exactly at** `id.timestamp + EXPIRY_TIME` is **valid**.

## Drifted restatement 1 — same file

[`messaging.md` invariants summary list](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/2049036afe878a7cb443f513f4e6ca453d90c340/specs/interop/messaging.md?plain=1#L127-L128):

> [Message Expiry Invariant]: The timestamp at the time of inclusion of the executing message MUST be **lower than** the initiating message timestamp (as defined in the [`Identifier`]) + `EXPIRY_TIME`.

`exec < init + EXPIRY_TIME` ⇒ the boundary case is **invalid**. Should read "lower than **or equal to**".

## Drifted restatement 2 — derivation.md

[`specs/interop/derivation.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/2049036afe878a7cb443f513f4e6ca453d90c340/specs/interop/derivation.md?plain=1#L34-L37):

> - `t > execution_timestamp - expiry_window`, where `expiry_window` is the expiry window in seconds.

At the boundary, `t > execution_timestamp - expiry_window` is `init > init` = false ⇒ **invalid**. Should be `t >= execution_timestamp - expiry_window` (validity `exec <= init + window` ⇔ `t >= execution_timestamp - expiry_window`).

## Implementations follow the normative definition

Both consensus implementations accept the boundary case (`exec == init + EXPIRY_TIME`):

- op-supernode: [`op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L192`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9e4981ed41d69cbb1a03f0af7d64d5e070d59e21/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L192) — rejects only on `execMsg.Timestamp + messageExpiryWindow < executingTimestamp`.
- kona: [`rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs#L406`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9e4981ed41d69cbb1a03f0af7d64d5e070d59e21/rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs#L406) — rejects only on `init < exec.saturating_sub(window)`.

## Suggested fix

Align both restatements to the normative § Message Expiry Invariant (they are summaries, the normative text and both implementations already agree): "lower than or equal to" in the messaging.md bullet, and `>=` in the derivation.md bullet.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude (Fable 5)*

topPRs.title: specs: replace flashblocks with subblocks
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Replace the detailed Flashblocks specification with a minimal, consumer-facing Subblocks specification.
- Document the WebSocket payload format, sequencing guarantees, JSON-RPC behavior, and transaction inclusion implications.
- Clarify that Subblocks are a backwards-compatible successor to Flashblocks, except that `state_root`, `block_hash`, `withdrawals_root`, and `withdrawals` are zeroed.
- Update the specs book summary and spelling dictionary.

## Related Issues
* Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/929

topPRs.title: holocene: require span batch overlap checks
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Require Holocene span batches to retain Delta's overlap checks before streaming singular batches. Clarify that only the remaining full span-batch checks are deferred.

Implementation: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22215

## Safety

This is a retroactive protocol change. It is expected to be safe because no production chain is known to have posted a span batch whose overlap disagreed with its safe chain. A follow-up should verify this assumption by scanning historical production channel data.

🤖 *Co-created with openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol*

topPRs.title: interop: Align expiry-boundary restatements with the normative invariant
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The message-expiry boundary is stated three times in the interop specs. The two summary restatements are one second stricter than the normative Message Expiry Invariant, which invalidates only `id.timestamp + EXPIRY_TIME < executing_block.timestamp` — so a message executed exactly at the boundary is valid.

This aligns both summaries with the normative text:

- `messaging.md` invariants list: "lower than" becomes "lower than or equal to".
- `derivation.md` invariants list: `t > execution_timestamp - expiry_window` becomes `>=`.

Both consensus implementations (op-supernode and kona) already accept the boundary case, so no implementation change is needed.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/specs#931
